en: In Kantian philosophy thinking, the infinite, the form of the objective is the first.

The absolute opposition of the same to the particular, finite, being is in the cognizing subject, but unconsciously or not at the same time objective for it; or one can also say, the absolute identity in which the opposition is sublated is purely objective, a mere thought — both are synonymous, for both, this form of absolute objectivity, the beyond of identity for cognition, and the subjective, cognition, into which the absolute opposition is placed, do not come together.

In Jacobi's philosophy the consciousness of the same is the first, and the opposition that is in cognition likewise flees, in order to represent it to itself as dissolved, to its opposite, a beyond of cognition.
But a middle is present between this transition to absolutely opposed things; but this middle is itself something subjective, a longing and a pain.

This longing is in Fichte's philosophy synthesized with Kantian objectivity, but not in such a way that the two opposed forms extinguished themselves in a true identity and indifference and the absolute middle emerged, but rather that Jacobian subjective union in the liveliness of the individual is itself only taken up into objective form.

In Kantian philosophy, on account of the contradiction of empty universality with living particularity, not the least grief shows itself; in the theoretical it is absolutely asserted, and in the practical, whose concept brings it with itself to sublate it, a formalism of jurisprudence and morality without liveliness as well as without truth appears.

Jacobi's philosophy has the being-identical of the universal and the particular in the — but subjective — individuality; such a union can therefore only be a grief and a longing, and the particularity must be something permanent, sanctified and absolute.

In Fichte this subjectivity of longing is itself made into the infinite, a thought thing, an absolute demand, and the demand is the culminating point of the system: I ought to be equal to not-I; but no point of indifference is to be cognized in it.
zh: 在康德哲学里，思维、无限者、客观东西的形式是第一位的。
同一个东西对特殊的、有限的、存在的东西的绝对对立，是在认识着的主体里，但却是无意识的，或者并不同时对它来说是客观的；或者也可以说，那种其中对立被扬弃了的绝对同一性纯粹是客观的，是一个单纯的思想，——两者是同一个意思，因为两者，即这种绝对客观性的形式、同一性对认识而言的彼岸，以及主观的东西、认识，绝对对立被置入其中，并不走到一起。
在雅可比哲学里，对同一个东西的意识是第一位的，而认识中的那个对立也同样逃向它的反面、逃向认识的一个彼岸，以便把对立设想为已经消解了的。
但在这种向绝对对立的东西的过渡之间存在着一个中间；但这个中间本身是某种主观的东西，一种渴望和一种痛苦。
这种渴望在费希特哲学里与康德的客观性综合在一起，但不是两个对立的形式在一种真正的同一性和无差别中相互熄灭、绝对中间浮现出来，而是雅可比那种在个体生命性中的主观统一本身只是被纳入到客观的形式里。
在康德哲学里，由于空洞的普遍性与活生生的特殊性之间的矛盾，丝毫不显露出苦恼；在理论的东西里，这个矛盾被绝对地断言，而在实践的东西里，后者的概念本身就带来要扬弃这个矛盾这件事，却出现了一种法学和道德的形式主义，既没有生命性，也没有真理。
雅可比哲学把普遍与特殊的同一存在放在——但却是主观的——个体性里；这样一种统一因此只能是一种苦恼和一种渴望，而特殊性必须是一种持久的、被神圣化的、绝对的东西。
在费希特那里，这种渴望的主观性本身被造成无限者，一个被思维的东西，绝对的应当要求，而这个要求是体系的顶点：我应当等于非我；但在它里面却看不出任何无差别点。

en: It has been recalled above how the system raises itself to the negative side of the absolute, infinity, to I as absolute thinking, and in this respect it is pure idealism, which, however, because that negative side is itself posited as the absolutely positive, becomes formal and has a realism standing over against it.

By the fact that it [is able] to equate the oppositions only in the infinite, i.e. makes abstracting thinking, pure activity opposed to being, into the absolute, it does not truly annihilate them, but this intellectual intuition is something formal, just like the idealism, and over against thinking reality appears, over against that identity of intellectual intuition the opposition appears, and all identity is the relative identity of the causal connection in a determining of the one by the other.
zh: 上面已经提到过，体系如何上升到绝对者的否定方面、即无限性，上升到作为绝对思维的我，就此而言它是纯粹的观念论，但这种观念论由于那个否定方面本身被设定为绝对肯定的东西，就变成形式的，并且有一个实在论与它相对立。
由于它[只能]在无限者中把那些对立等同起来，也就是说，把抽象化思维、把与存在相对立的纯粹活动造成绝对者，它并没有真正地消灭这些对立，而这种智性直观是某种形式的东西，正如观念论一样，并且与思维相对，实在性出现了，与智性直观的那种同一性相对，对立出现了，而一切同一性都是因果联系的那种相对的同一性，即一方被另一方规定。

en: According to the task of philosophy as it has been determined by the Lockean and Humean culture, the world is to be calculated and then explained from the standpoint of the subject; into this world to be explained there is carried precisely this opposition that takes place between it and the subject: it divides itself into an ideal and a real side, so that the ideal, in the relative opposition to the real, becomes at one time the pure identity abstracting from reality or the pure concept, at another time, however, that which is related to reality, space, time, categories, the ideality of the real.

The objective or universal of the real now consists solely in that which in the division of the world is the ideal side, so that the idealism that sets out to explain the objective world, immediately, in having cognized objectivity as the ideal, has also derived it from the principle of the ideal, of the I, of the universal, which in opposition to the world generally is the subject, and has thereby sublated the being-in-and-for-itself of the objective.

This critical idealism, which Fichte brought out in sharper outline, is, as is self-evident, something formal: the universal of the world opposed to the subject is posited as universal, ideal, as thinking and thereby as I; but the particular necessarily remains behind, and if, according to the fashionable position of the idea of philosophy, there is to be talk of explanation, then of the objective world the most interesting side, the side of its reality, remains unexplained.

That the real, as [that which is] for sensation, is something empirical and under this title is straightaway thrown away and declared unworthy of consideration, as Kant does, is just as little satisfying as when Fichte shows that sensation is absolutely something subjective and that red etc. is first spread upon the surface by the hand of the subject and thereby receives objectivity.
For the question is precisely not about ideality but about reality, and it is indifferent whether reality is an infinite multitude of sensations or of properties of things.

In the practical part of the Doctrine of Science, to be sure, the air is assumed as if the absolute reality for the ideal side, the things as they are in themselves, were to have been constructed out of the way we ought to make them; but there nothing is derived except an analysis of the concept of striving and of impulse in an intelligence and a few concepts of reflection for the feeling that feelings must be different; but of the task of constructing the system of things as they ought to be, nothing but the formal concept of ought is analyzed, but apart from this formal essence feeling itself as a real system or the totality of ought is not constructed in the least, for already in and for itself ought admits absolutely no totality, but the manifoldness of reality appears as an incomprehensible, original determinacy and empirical necessity; particularity and difference as such is something absolute.

The standpoint for this reality is the empirical standpoint of every single individual, and for every single individual his reality is the incomprehensible sphere of common actuality, into which he is once and for all enclosed.

It need not be recalled how indifferent to this absoluteness of the empirical that formal idealism is, which proves that this whole empirical reality is only something subjective, a feeling, for this form changes not the least in the common and incomprehensible necessity of empirical determinate being; and there is absolutely no thinking of a true ideality of actuality and of the real side, whether they now appear as property of things or as sensation.
zh: 按照哲学的任务，正如它被洛克式和休谟式的文化所规定的那样，从主体的立场出发，世界应当被计算，并且现在应当得到说明；正是在这个有待说明的世界里，被带入了它和主体之间发生的那种对立：这个世界分成一个观念的方面和一个实在的方面，以致观念物在与实在物的相对对立中，时而成为纯粹的、从实在性中抽象出来的同一性，或纯粹的概念，时而又成为与实在性相关的东西，即空间、时间、范畴，即实在物的观念性。
实在物的客观东西或普遍东西，现在仅仅在于世界分裂中那个观念的方面，以致那种着手说明客观世界的观念论，在它把客观性认作观念物之后，就立刻从观念物的原则、从我的原则、从普遍东西的原则——后者在与世界对立时一般就是主体——把客观性推导出来，并由此扬弃了客观东西的自在自为存在。
这种批判的观念论，费希特把它以更鲜明的轮廓提了出来，正如自己就会明白的那样，是某种形式的东西：与主体相对立的世界的那种普遍东西，被设定为普遍东西、观念物，被设定为思维，并因此被设定为我；但特殊的东西必然留在后面，而如果按照哲学观念那种受人偏爱的立场要谈说明，那么客观世界最有趣的那个方面、即它的实在性那个方面，仍然得不到说明。
说实在物作为感觉所面对的东西是某种经验的东西，并且在这个名目下干脆被扔掉、被宣布为不值得考察，就像康德所做的那样，这跟费希特表明感觉绝对说来是某种主观的东西、并且红等等是由主体的手才散布到平面上、由此获得客观性一样，都不令人满意。
因为问题恰恰不在于观念性，而在于实在性，而实在性究竟是无限多的感觉还是无限多的物的性状，这是无所谓的。

在《知识学》的实践部分里，虽然摆出一副样子，好像对观念的方面来说绝对实在性、即物自身的样子，本来应当从我们应当把它们造成什么样子中建构出来；但那里所推导出来的无非是对一种智性中努力和冲动的概念的一种分析，以及为了感觉而得出的一些反思概念，即感觉必然各不相同；然而就建构物应当如何的那个体系这一任务而言，被分析的不过是应当的形式概念，而除了这个形式本质之外，感觉本身作为实在的体系或者说应当的总体性，也丝毫没有得到建构，因为应当本来就自在自为地根本不允许有总体性，而实在性的杂多反而显得是一种不可把握的、原初的规定性和经验的必然性；特殊性和差别本身则是某种绝对的东西。
这种实在性的立场是每一个个别个体的经验立场，而对每一个个别个体来说，他的实在性就是普通现实性那个不可把握的领域，他反正就被关在其中。
不必提醒人们，那种形式的观念论对这种经验东西的绝对性是多么无所谓，它证明这整个经验的实在性只是某种主观的东西、一种感觉，因为这种形式在经验的定在那种普通而不可把握的必然性上丝毫也没有改变什么；而根本不能去设想现实性和实在方面有什么真正的观念性，无论它们表现为物的性状还是表现为感觉。

en: The formalism of the knowledge here called idealistic, which has been developed in Jacobi's philosophy, which has the most determinate and most open consciousness of it, actually needs no further explanations in Fichte's philosophy, which shares it with the others through the principle of subjectivity, and that the absolute identity is not for cognition and knowledge but only for faith.

The essential thing about it is that the pure concept, empty thinking, is added to a content, a determinacy of the concept, or conversely determinacy is added to indeterminacy, in an incomprehensible way.

Whether according to Jacobi's dogmatism the objective, the given, is called the first, to which the concept later adds itself, or whether Fichte makes empty knowledge, I, the first, whose essence is the same as the empty understanding of analyzing knowledge, namely an identity for which in Fichte the determinacy foreign to it, not to be comprehended out of it, appears as the later, makes not the least difference in the matter.
zh: 这里被称作观念论的那种知识的形式主义——它是在雅可比哲学里展开的，而雅可比哲学对这一点有着最确定、最公开的意识——在费希特哲学里其实不需要进一步的说明，因为费希特哲学通过主体性的原则，并且通过绝对同一性不是为认识和知识、而只是为信仰而存在这一点，与那些哲学共有这种形式主义。
它的本质在于，纯粹的概念、空洞的思维以一种不可把握的方式加到一个内容、一个概念的规定性上，或者反过来，规定性加到无规定性上。
无论是按照雅可比的独断论，把客观的东西、被给予的东西称为第一位的，概念后来才加到它上面，还是费希特把空洞的知识、我造成第一位的，而后者的本质与分析的知识那种空洞的知性是同一个东西，即一种同一性，在费希特那里，对这种同一性来说，与它相异、不能从它出发以概念把握的规定性表现为后来者，这在事情上丝毫不造成区别。

en: If according to Fichte's idealism the I does not sense and intuit things, but only intuits its sensing and its intuiting and only knows of its knowing, then pure empty activity, purely free acting, is the first and only certain thing, and there is absolutely nothing but pure knowing and pure intuiting and sensing, I = I.

We shall see later how through the absolute act of will the whole annihilated world of sense receives reality at all; but the knowledge of this reality, the relation of the absolute emptiness and indeterminacy of knowledge to the determinacy and to that reality, is the incomprehensible, and the one is as foreign to the other, the particular as foreign to the universal, as Jacobi's empirically given determinacy is to indeterminacy or to the concept of the analyzing understanding.

Fichte's way of knowing only of knowledge, namely only of the empty identity, prepared for itself, however, through its own formalism, a way to the particular; it is acknowledged that the sole truth and certainty, pure self-consciousness and pure knowing, is something incomplete, conditioned by something else, i.e. that the absolute of the system is not absolute and precisely for that reason must be proceeded to something else.
This recognized incompleteness of the absolute principle and the necessity, recognized therefrom, of a proceeding to something else, is the principle of the deduction of the world of sense.

The completely empty, with which a beginning is made, has through its absolute lack the advantage of bearing in itself immanently the immediate necessity of filling itself, of having to proceed to something else and from this something else to other others into an infinite objective world.

Is there then a higher apriority of a principle than in which the necessity of the whole lies immediately? — a necessity that rests on the fact that the principle is absolutely a part and through its infinite poverty is the infinite possibility of wealth.

The principle plays in this way the doubled role of being at one time absolute, at another time absolutely finite, and in the last quality being able to become a starting point for the whole empirical infinity.
zh: 如果按照费希特的观念论，我不是感觉和直观物，而只是直观自己的感觉和自己的直观，并且只知道自己的知识，那么纯粹空洞的活动、纯粹自由的行为就是第一位的、唯一确定的东西，而绝对说来除了纯粹的知识、纯粹的直观和感觉之外什么也没有，我 = 我。
我们后面会看到，整个被消灭的感性世界如何通过绝对的意志行为一般地获得实在性；但对这种实在性的知识、知识的绝对空洞性和无规定性与规定性以及那种实在性的关系，却是不可把握的东西，而且一方对另一方、特殊的东西对普遍的东西，就像雅可比经验地被给予的规定性对无规定性、或对分析着的知性的概念一样，同样是相异的。
费希特那种只知道知识、也就是只知道空洞同一性的方式，却通过它自己的形式主义为自己准备了一条通往特殊东西的道路；人们承认，唯一的真理和确定性、纯粹自我意识和纯粹知识，是某种不完满的、被别的东西制约的东西，也就是说，体系的绝对者并不是绝对的，正因为如此才必须前进到别的东西。
这种被认识到的绝对原则的不完满性，以及由此认识到的前进到别的东西的必然性，就是感性世界演绎的原则。
那个完全空洞的东西，即人们由之开始的东西，由于它的绝对缺乏而有这样一个优点：它内在地带有一种直接的必然性，即必须充实自己，必须前进到一个别的东西，并且从这个别的东西前进到另一些别的东西，进入一个无限的客观世界。
那么，还有比这样一种原则更高的先验性吗，即整体的必然性直接就落在它里面？——一种必然性，它基于：原则绝对说来是部分，并且通过它无限的贫乏而是财富的无限可能性。
原则以这种方式扮演双重角色：时而绝对，时而绝对说来是有限的，并且在最后一种性质上能够成为整个经验无限性的一个起点。

en: The formalism of this principle has, considered for itself, also the great advantage that it is easy to make intelligible.

There has been general complaint about the hard demand of intellectual intuition, and in its time it was told that people, in the very attempt to produce the pure act of will and intellectual intuition, had fallen into madness; both were without doubt occasioned by the name of the thing, which Fichte describes as simple and common enough and of which it was presumably only with difficulty that one could convince oneself that it really was only this common and simple thing.

To intuit some thing, something foreign to pure consciousness or the I, which according to Fichte's expression is likewise given in common consciousness, is empirical intuition; but to abstract from everything foreign in consciousness and to think oneself, is intellectual intuition.

To abstract, in any knowledge, from all determinate content and to know only pure knowledge, the purely formal element of it, is pure absolute knowing; after all, this abstraction is easy to make, and everyone also knows something on which he can make the abstraction.

But on account of that from which one has abstracted, one also has no need to be anxious, for it does not get lost, but rather enters again for knowledge — and for action anyway — in its whole empirical extension and breadth; only philosophy makes this contingency of common consciousness methodical, but without taking from it in the least anything of its contingency and commonness.
zh: 这个原则的形式主义，就它自身来看，也有一个大好处，就是它很容易让人明白。
人们普遍在抱怨智性直观这个苛刻的要求，当时还传说，有人在着手产生纯粹意志行动和智性直观的时候陷入了疯狂；这两件事无疑都是由这事情的名称引起的，费希特把这事情描述得足够简单和平常，而关于它，恐怕很难让人相信它真的只是这个平常而简单的东西。
直观某一个物，直观某种对纯粹意识或我来说是异己的东西——而这纯粹意识或我，按照费希特的说法，在平常意识里也同样是被给予的——，这是经验直观；但从意识中一切异己的东西抽象出来并思维自己，则是智性直观。
在任何一种知识里从一切确定的内容抽象出来，并且只知道纯粹知识、只知道它之中纯粹形式的东西，这就是纯粹的绝对知识；这种抽象毕竟容易做，而每个人也都知道一点东西，让他可以在上面做这种抽象。
但关于人们所抽象掉的那个东西，人们也不必担心，因为它并没有丢失，反而会以其全部经验的广度和宽度重新进入知识——而对行动来说本来就是这样——；只不过哲学把平常意识的这种偶然性弄成方法性的，却丝毫不减损它的偶然性和平常性。

en: The methodical element of this knowledge, or philosophy about common consciousness, consists in this, that first of all one starts from something absolutely true and certain, from the I, from knowledge itself in all knowledge, from pure consciousness.

But since it proves itself as principle of deduction immediately only by being absolutely incomplete and purely finite, its truth and certainty is of such a kind as philosophy rejects; for philosophy holds truth and certainty to be solely in what is not incomplete, nor an abstraction, nor conditioned.
zh: 这种知识的方法性的东西，或者说关于平常意识的哲学，就在于：首先从某种绝对真的和确定的东西出发，从我出发，从一切知识中的知识本身出发，从纯粹意识出发。
但是，既然它之所以直接表明自己是演绎的原则，只是靠它绝对不完整并且纯粹有限，那么它的真理和确定性就是这样一种，哲学把它抛弃掉；因为在哲学看来，真理和确定性只在于那不完整、不是抽象、也不受条件限制的东西里。

en: But that the emptiness of knowledge becomes the principle of the progression — this is found precisely in the fact that the same is something absolutely defective and therefore immediately needs another and becomes the point of attachment for another, which is the condition of the same.

The form under which the objective world steps in as something foreign to that which is completed by it, namely to pure knowledge, is the inference from the lack of a circumstance in the point of attachment to its necessity, from the incompleteness of the absolute, which is itself a part, to another part that completes the former.

But that in what is posited as absolute there is a lack, that it is only a part — this unity is possible solely through the idea of totality, or generally only through the consciousness that for the sake of the so-called intellectual intuition, of thinking oneself and of pure knowledge, abstraction has been made from other foreign material, which is afterwards taken up again.

Why it is not that idea of totality itself, measured against which pure knowledge shows itself as something incomplete, that comes on the scene as the absolute, but rather something acknowledged as part and defective — for this no ground can be discerned in itself, except that this part has empirical certainty and truth, since after all everyone knows that he knows; such empirical truth is given preference over the absolute truth of totality.

But the inference onward from the part to other parts is nothing but a resumption of that from which abstraction has been made; or, since what has come about through the abstraction stands immediately in a negative relation to that from which abstraction is made, the same is present in the former, though in negative form, the deduction is nothing but a transformation of signs, of minus into plus.

In pure knowledge the world of sense is posited as a minus, abstraction has been made from it, it has been negated; the inference to it consists in this, that it is now posited as a plus and this plus as the condition of self-consciousness.

In the freedom of the rational being, the objective element toward which its freedom is directed is posited as a minus: the deduction of the sphere for freedom thus consists in this, that it is posited with a plus, as existing, just as an empty purse is a purse in relation to which money is indeed already posited, but with the sign minus, and the money can be immediately deduced from it, because it is immediately posited in its lack.
zh: 但知识的空洞会成为进程的原则，这一点恰恰在于：这知识是一种绝对有缺陷的东西，因而直接需要另一个东西，并成为另一个东西的连接点，而这另一个东西是它的条件。
客观世界作为某种异己的东西，加进那个靠它才得以完备的东西、即纯粹知识时所采取的形式，就是从连接点上某个情况的缺失推出它的必然性，从绝对者的不完整——这绝对者本身是一个部分——推出另一个部分，而这另一个部分使前一个部分完备。
但是，在那被设定为绝对的东西里有一个缺失，它只是一个部分——这种统一只有通过总体性的观念才可能，或者根本只有通过这样一种意识才可能：为了所谓的智性直观、为了思维自己、为了纯粹知识，人们从别的异己的东西抽象掉了，而那别的异己的东西事后又被重新接纳进来。
为什么出场为绝对者的不是那个总体性的观念本身——以它来衡量，纯粹知识显出自己是某种不完整的东西——，而是一个被承认为部分并且有缺陷的东西，这本身看不出有什么理由，除非是因为这个部分具有经验的确定性和真理，毕竟每个人都知道自己知道；人们把偏爱给了这种经验的真理，而不给总体性的绝对真理。
然而，从部分往前推论到其他部分，无非是把被抽象掉的东西重新接纳回来；或者，既然通过抽象而产生出来的东西直接处于同被抽象掉的东西的否定关系之中，那被抽象掉的东西就在前者里，只是以否定的形式存在，那么演绎无非是一种符号的转换，即把减号转换成加号。
在纯粹知识里，感性世界被设定为一个减号，人们从它抽象掉了，它被否定了；向它的推论就在于：它现在被设定为一个加号，而这个加号被设定为自我意识的条件。
在理性存在者的自由里，它的自由所指向的客观东西被设定为一个减号：所以，为自由而作的那个领域的演绎就在于，它带着一个加号、即作为存在着的而被设定，就像一个空钱袋是一个钱袋，相对于这个钱袋，钱当然已经被设定了，不过带着减号，而钱可以直接从这个钱袋里演绎出来，因为它就设定在这钱袋的缺失之中。

en: A cognition through such deduction is in and for itself no true cognition; for this begins from the absolute, which is neither a part, nor incomplete, nor certainty and truth for empirical knowledge alone, nor through abstraction, but through true intellectual intuition.

That cognition out of the lack rests at bottom on the very same givenness of the objects for analysing thought as that with which Jacobi, Köppen and others find the manifold and its interconnection in the revealed and believed facts of consciousness — only that what is found has a positive sign in Jacobi and Köppen, but in Fichte a negative sign; the former find the very same thing as present which Fichte finds as lacking.

This idealism is therefore the true inversion of formal knowledge — but not, as Jacobi214) said, of the cube of Spinozism; for Spinoza's cube is not invertible, because it floats in the free ether and there is in it no above nor below, much less any sphere or tortoise on which it would be founded, but it has its rest and its ground in itself, is its own sphere and tortoise.
By contrast, the irregular polyhedron of formal knowledge lies on an earth foreign to it, in which it has its root and on which it has its support; for it, therefore, there is an above and a below.
Ordinary formal knowledge has manifold empirical knowledge as ground, but draws out of it, into the ideal atmosphere, manifold peaks of concepts.

Fichte's formal knowledge is an inversion of that; it begins in the atmosphere, in which one and the same is found only negatively and ideally, and, conscious of the ideality of the same, it lowers the negatively present content with a positive sign as reality.
zh: 通过这样一种演绎的认识，自在自为都不是真正的认识；因为这种认识从绝对者开始，而绝对者既不是部分，也不残缺，也不是仅仅对经验才有确定性和真理，也不是通过抽象，而是通过真正的智性直观。
那种从缺失出发的认识，归根到底依据的是对象对于进行分析的思维的同一种被给予性，就像雅可比、科彭等人在意识那些被启示和被信仰的事实里找到杂多的东西及其联结一样——只不过所找到的东西在雅可比和科彭那里带着肯定的符号，在费希特这里却带着否定的符号；前两人把费希特发现为缺失的东西恰恰发现为现成的。
所以，这种观念论是形式知识的真正颠倒——但不是像雅可比214)所说的那样，是斯宾诺莎主义的立方体的颠倒；因为斯宾诺莎的立方体不可颠倒，它漂浮在自由的以太里，在它上面既没有上也没有下，更没有什么球或乌龟可以作为它奠基于其上的东西，相反，它在自身之中有它的静止和根据，它自己就是自己的球和乌龟。
相反，形式知识那个无规则的多面体则躺在一块对它来说是异己的大地上，它在这大地上有它的根，在这大地上有它的支撑；所以对它来说就有上和下。
通常的形式知识以杂多的经验为根据，但它从经验中抽取出杂多的概念尖端，进入观念的大气层。
费希特的形式知识是前一种的颠倒；它从那种大气层开始，在那里，同一个东西只被否定地、观念地找到，而它意识到这同一个东西的观念性，就把那否定地现成的内容带着肯定的符号作为实在性沉降下来。

en: As regards now the product of such a cognition, which begins from the certain part and in the progression through the parts wants gradually to express the lack as a totality posited for knowledge, it seems that the product not only can be the totality, but also must be it.
For its idea seems to be the presupposed, since through it alone it can be cognized that that absolutely certain first is only a part.

Since it is thus truly the first, the progression of the development seems to have to present it; but that the whole of this progression is totality is impossible precisely because something cognized as part, as defective, is supposed to have absolute truth and certainty.

Pure empirical knowledge, which knows nothing of a part, does not fix the part through reflection as something absolutely having essence, is indeed able to begin from a part and through its progression through the parts to describe and present the whole circle; for because it is empirical knowledge, it does not stick in the fetters of reflection, which makes the part into an in-itself and so makes it impossible to arrive at the whole.

But a totality produced, or rather found, by empirical knowledge is, even if it is given to representation as such, not for cognition; for cognition the parts must be absolutely determined by the whole, the whole must be the first of cognition.

That formal cognition, which converts the negatively found into something positive, just as little as it begins from the whole but goes on from part to parts, is able to come out of its part-nature neither for representation in general nor for cognition.

For if, in the fact that it cognizes empty knowledge as something incomplete, the absolute idea seems to float before it, this idea immediately signifies only the negativity of an other, which is necessary and which itself in turn is only a finite thing, a part is an other, and so on into the infinite; it proves itself to be something absolutely formal, because the finite point of attachment, thus the part, is an in-itself, an absolute, whereby every true idea of totality is absolutely destroyed.

What the deduction produces through its trick of converting the negative into a positive is therefore necessarily precisely that mass of common empirical reality, a nature finite everywhere, a world of sense; through the abstraction from the foreign in the I, no speculative abstraction had been made from it, i.e. it had not been annihilated, but the same formula had been posited in the very same connection and the same common actuality, only with a negative sign in the form of a lack.

As the mirror had received them in common empiricism and posited them ideally in itself, so it afterwards gives them back again, and this giving back, or to name that which the lack lacks, is called an immanent, transcendental deduction.
zh: 至于这样一种认识的产物——这种认识从确定的部分开始，并在沿各个部分前进的过程中逐步想把缺失说成一种为知识而设定的总体性——，看来这产物不仅能够是总体性，而且必须是总体性。
因为它的观念似乎是被预设的东西，只有通过这观念才能认识到，那绝对确定的第一个东西只是一个部分。
既然它才是真正的第一个东西，那么发展的进程似乎就必须把它展示出来；但是，这个进程的整体是总体性，这恰恰由于一个被认识为部分、有缺陷的东西竟然应当具有绝对的真理和确定性，而是不可能的。
纯粹经验并不知道什么部分，也不通过反思把部分固定为某种绝对具有本质的东西，它倒是有能力从一个部分开始，并通过它沿各个部分的前进，描述和展示出整个圆圈；因为它是经验，它就没有卡在反思的脚镣里，而反思把部分弄成一个自在的东西，于是使人无法达到整体。
但是，由经验产生出来、或者更确切地说是由经验找到的总体性，即使它作为这样的东西被给予表象，也不是为认识的；因为对认识来说，各个部分必须绝对由整体来规定，整体必须是认识的第一者。
那种形式性的、把否定地找到的东西转变为肯定东西的认识，既然它不是从整体开始，而是从部分走向部分，它就无法从它的部分本质中走出来，既不能为一般表象走出来，也不能为认识走出来。
因为，如果说它由于把空洞的知识认作某种不完整的东西，而似乎有绝对的观念浮现在眼前，那么这观念直接只意味着一个他者的否定性，而这个他者是必需的，它本身又只是一个有限的东西，一个部分是另一个东西，如此以至无限；它表明自己是某种绝对形式性的东西，因为那有限的连接点、也就是部分，是一个自在的东西，是一个绝对者，于是总体性的一切真的观念都被绝对地毁掉了。
所以，演绎靠它那套把否定东西转换成肯定东西的把戏所产生出来的，必然恰恰就是那一堆平常的经验实在性，一个处处有限的自然，一个感性世界；通过从自我中异己的东西抽象掉，人们并没有思辨地把它抽象掉，即并没有把它消灭掉，而只是把同一个公式在完全同一个联系和同一个平常现实性中、仅仅带着否定的符号以缺失的形式设定下来。
正如镜子在平常的经验主义中接纳了它们并把它们观念地设定在自身之中，它事后又把它们交还回来，而这种交还——或者说，把缺失所缺失的那个东西说出来——就叫作一种内在的、先验的演绎。

en: Since the finitude of the starting point, which is absolute, makes it impossible that the birth of cognition be a true whole — for this whole is possible only through the fact that no part is in itself —, a true ideal, in which the finitude of empirical reality would vanish, affection would become nature, is absolutely impossible.
There is no fullness of representations other than that of finite ones; nature is absolutely the world of sense.

The change that takes place with common empiricism is that it has been deduced, i.e. that the system, or rather the mass — for a system is not to be thought of — of the representations necessary for common consciousness first appears as pure lack and attached to that which is the subject of this lack, namely the I, and it is optional to reflect now on the pure lack, now on the mass of what is lacking, now to think pure knowing, and always pure knowing, the emptiness, the nothing, but now the whole content of this nothing as a mass of subjective, but only subjective, affections.

Both, the pure minus and that of which the I is deprived in order that there be a lack, are inseparable; for the abstraction is immediate only through the fact that it stands in relation to that from which abstraction is made, or that this is posited with a negative sign.
Theoretical science, now, consists in the cognition of the lack and of the manifold of which it is deprived; but the proper reality, the true plus, it receives only through the pure act of will.
But the one is never without the other, emptiness not without that of which it is empty, whether this be posited ideally or really, subjectively or objectively.
zh: 由于起点——它是绝对的——的有限性使认识的诞生不可能是一个真正的整体——因为这个整体只有靠没有任何部分是自在的才是可能的——，所以，一个真的观念，在其中经验实在性的有限性会消失、刺激会变成自然，是绝对不可能的。
除了有限的表象的丰盈之外，没有别的表象的丰盈；自然绝对就是感性世界。
平常经验主义所发生的变化，就是它被演绎了，也就是说，为平常意识所必需的那些表象的体系——或者不如说那一堆东西，因为根本谈不上一个体系——首先被设定为纯粹的缺失，并且显得被连接在那种是这一缺失的主体、即我之上，而人们尽可随意地时而反思纯粹的缺失，时而反思缺失着的东西那一堆，时而思维纯粹的知识、并且永远只是纯粹的知识、空洞、无，时而则把这个无的全部内容思维为一堆主观的、但只是主观的刺激。
两者，纯粹的减号和那个我有所缺失、从而才有一个缺失的东西，是不可分离的；因为抽象之为直接的，仅仅在于它与被抽象掉的东西处在关联中，或者说，在于后者被带着否定的符号设定下来。
理论科学现在就在于对缺失以及被缺失的杂多的认识；但它只有通过纯粹的意志行动才获得本来意义上的实在性，即真正的加号。
但一方从来离不开另一方，空洞离不开它所空的那个东西，不论这东西现在是被设定为观念的或实在的、主观的或客观的。

en: The I, who in the second act of the Vocation of Man215), to which presentation we want here above all to hold, has himself set into freedom by a spirit, does not, when at the end he believes himself really set into freedom, think at all of this complete connectedness of his with empirical necessity and of the incomprehensible sphere of his common reality in feeling; in passing, on S. 88, to the spirit's question: "You surely never feel in general?" — he gives the answer: "I: By no means.
Every sensation is a determinate one.

One never merely sees or feels or hears, but always something determinate, the red, green, blue colour, the cold, warm, smooth, rough, the sound of the violin, the voice of man and the like" (this like no doubt comprises the rest of nature, but the exquisite part of it is supposed to be named in what is expressly listed, the green, red, the violin sound; among the determinacies, however, examples of determinate forms would have been more interesting and more serviceable than those examples of the formless) "seen, felt, heard.
Let that be settled between us."

From all this determinate [content] and from the determinacy of his empirical existence in general, the I believes himself freed without further ado by the fact that he is convinced that those determinacies are in him and are only his affections, that the knowing of them is an immediate knowing of his state, and that the whole chain of common necessity is only one-sided, that he is free, therefore, by the fact that the subject is, for itself, through affections and not through things, an absolutely empirical being, — a contradiction which is to be counted among the hardest.

For the sake of the conviction that the consciousness of a thing outside us is absolutely nothing further than the product of our own faculty of representation, the spirit declares the I free and eternally redeemed from the fear that humiliated and tormented him, free from a necessity that is supposed to be only in his thinking, and from the actuality of things that exist outside him, — as if he were not in one and the same captivity of his state, in one and the same necessity which, although it is no longer present in the form of his thinking as an outer object, exists with just the same actuality, arbitrariness and contingency as a series of affections and states.
zh: 这个我，在《人的使命》215)的第二幕里——我们在这里主要想依据的就是这个表述——，让自己由一个精神置入自由之中，当他在最后真的相信自己已被置入自由之中时，根本不去想他与经验必然性的这种完全联结，也不去想他在情感中那种平常实在性的不可把握的领域；他顺带在 S. 88 上，对精神的提问“你毕竟从来不是一般地感觉吧？”——给出了回答：“我：绝不。
每一种感觉都是确定的。
人们从来不是仅仅看、感觉或听，而总是看、感觉、听到某种确定的东西，红的、绿的、蓝的颜色，冷的、暖的、光滑的、粗糙的，小提琴的声音、人的嗓音之类”（这个“之类”大概涵盖了自然的其余部分，而其中精致的东西，据说应当在那些被逐一列举的东西——绿、红、小提琴的声音——里得到命名；不过在这些规定性中，确定形式的例子本会比那些无形式的例子更有趣、更合用）“看、感觉、听到。
这就算我们之间说定了。”
对于这一切确定的东西，以及他的经验存在一般的规定性，这个我径直认为自己已经由此摆脱出来了，因为他确信：那些规定性是在他之中，并且只是他的刺激，关于它们的有知是对他的状态的一种直接的有知，而平常必然性的整条链条只是片面的，他之所以自由，就在于主体对自己来说是通过刺激、而不是通过物而成为一个绝对经验性的本质，——这是一个必须算在最坚硬者之列的矛盾。

为了那种确信——即对一个在我们之外的物的意识，绝对无非是我们自己的表象能力的产物——，精神宣布这个我是自由的，并且永远从那种使他屈辱、折磨他的恐惧中得到解救，从一种据说只在他的思维中的必然性中得到解救，也从在他之外存在的诸物的现实性中得到解救，——就好像他并不是处在同一种他自身状态的囚禁中、处在同一种必然性中，这种必然性尽管不再作为外在客体出现在他的思维形式里，却以同样的现实性、任意性和偶然性作为一连串刺激和状态而存在。

en: Since, then, the I is still endowed with one and the same wealth of the realities as sensations, it is not to be comprehended how, over the Façon of thinghood that his system of affections has lost, he can fall into the lamenting that now nothing, absolutely nothing, is supposed to be but representations, determinations of a consciousness as mere consciousness.

Not about what he lost — for that mere Façon of the objectivity and corporeality of the sweet and bitter is not worth the trouble — but about the fact that he remains rich in his uninjured necessity in its whole length and breadth of sweet and bitter and red etc. sensation and of the naked fact of intuition (S. 169), to which the thing, which alone has been lost to him, is added only through thinking, — had he to lament; not about what the spirit took, but about the whole finitude that it left him, could the I call it a wicked spirit.
zh: 既然这个我依然被赋予同一种丰盈的、作为感觉的诸实在性，那就不能理解，他怎么会因为他的刺激体系所失去的物性那种 Façon（样式），而陷入这样的哀叹：如今除了表象，即作为单纯意识的一种意识的规定之外，什么都没有，绝对什么都没有。
不是对他所失去的东西——因为甜和苦那种单纯的客观性和形体性的 Façon 不值得费这点力气——，而是对他依然富有的、未受损伤的必然性，即甜、苦、红等等感觉以及直观的赤裸事实（S. 169）的整个长和宽——只有通过思维，那个唯独对他失去了的物才加到它们上面——，他要哀叹；不是由于精神拿走了什么，而是由于精神留给他的整个有限性，这个我才能把精神叫作一个邪恶的精神。

en: The immediate product of this formal idealism, which has arisen for us, thus presents itself in the following shape: a realm of unity-less empirical knowledge and purely contingent manifoldness stands over against an empty thinking.

If empty thinking is posited as an efficacious and real force, it must, like the rest of objectivity, be cognised as something ideal; or, in order to have the opposition to empirical necessity and manifoldness purely, it must be posited not as a real efficacious force, i.e. in relation to reality, but purely for itself, as empty unity, as universality wholly separated from particularity.
Kant's pure reason is precisely this empty thinking, and reality [is] likewise opposed to that empty identity, and it is the non-agreement of the two that makes the beyond-faith necessary.

But the reality that necessarily lacks identity with practical reason is in the Kantian philosophy considered not merely in the wholly merely empirical relation in which it is present as sensation of the empirical subject and can alone occur in the Fichtean idealism, but Kant cognises it at the same time as a higher reality, namely as organic system and beautiful nature.

In that the Kantian idealism loses the purity of abstraction for this — an abstraction which sets identity wholly out of difference and opposed to it, as one member of the opposition, and the other as pure empirical necessity and a manifoldness lacking all identity —, it gains against this formalism through the fact that at one place of the system the speculative idea emerges more.
zh: 这个形式观念论——它对我们已经产生出来了——的直接产物，于是呈现出这样的形态：一个无统一的经验、纯属偶然的杂多的王国，与一种空洞的思维相对而立。
如果空洞的思维被设定为起作用的、实在的力量，那它就必须像其余客观性一样被认作观念物；或者，为了纯粹地拥有与经验必然性和杂多的对立，它就不应当被设定为实在的、起作用的力量，即不应当被设定在与实在性的关联中，而应当纯粹自为地、作为空洞的统一性、作为与特殊性完全分离的普遍性被设定。
康德的纯粹理性正是这种空洞的思维，而实在性[是]也同样与那种空洞的同一性相对立的，并且正是两者的不相一致，才使那个彼岸的信仰成为必然。
但那种必然缺乏与实践理性之同一性的实在性，在康德哲学中并不只是在完全纯粹经验的关联中被考察——在这种关联中，它作为经验主体的感觉而存在，并且只能在费希特观念论中出现——，相反，康德同时把它认识为一种更高的实在性，即认作有机的体系和美的自然。
康德观念论为此失去了抽象的纯粹性——这种抽象把同一性完全从差别中取出来并与之相对立，把它设定为对立的一个环节，把另一者设定为纯粹的经验必然性和一种完全缺乏同一性的杂多——，但它由此赢得了对抗这种形式主义的东西，因为在体系的一个地方，思辨的观念更多地显露出来。

en: In this way, in the Fichtean idealism the system of knowing is a knowing of a wholly empty knowing, to which an empirical reality — while to the unity the manifoldness is opposed — is absolutely opposed, and of a relative identity of the two.

To such a formal knowing, which can bring it no further than to relative identity, and to its absolute opposition, which in Kant has the popular and less abstract form of happiness and morality, the true identity must stand opposed as an absolute beyond.
Because thinking and knowing are absolutely only formal, only in opposition, only relative, rational cognition and the speculative idea are immediately sublated and impossible.

The highest exertion of formal thinking is the recognition of its nothing and of the ought; but because it does not truly give itself up, the ought is perennial; it is a lasting willing that can do nothing but break through only up to infinity and to the nothing, but not through the same to positive rational cognition.
zh: 这样一来，在费希特观念论中，知识的体系就是一种关于完全空洞的知识的知识——与这种知识绝对对立的是经验的实在性，而与统一性相对立的则是杂多——，也是一种关于两者相对同一性的知识。
面对这样一种形式的知识——它只能达到相对的同一性为止——以及它的绝对对立——这种对立在康德那里具有幸福和道德那种通俗而较少抽象的形式——，真正的同一性必然作为一个绝对的彼岸与之相对而立。
因为思维和知识绝对只是形式的、只是在对立中、只是相对的，所以理性的认识和思辨的观念直接就被扬弃了，并且是不可能的。
形式思维最高的努力，就是承认它的无和应当；但因为它并没有真正地放弃自身，所以应当是永续的；它是一种持续着的意愿，它做不了别的，只能一直冲到无限性和无那里，却不能穿过这无而突破到肯定的理性认识。

en: This form of the triad: positing, thinking, infinity — then being, counter-positing, finitude and a — since the first two are absolutely different — relation of both to one another for knowing, which itself is a doubled one, a) an imperfect, the positive relation for knowing, b) absolute identity of both (and this is outside such a knowing and cognising) — this form of the triad the whole system expresses in all its presentations as first in the Doctrine of Science.
zh: 这种三元的形式：设定、思维、无限性，——接着是存在、设立对立、有限性和一种——由于前两个是绝对不同的——两者为知识而相互的关系，这种关系本身又是双重的，a) 一种不完满的、为知识而有的肯定关系，b) 两者的绝对同一性（而这种同一性在这样的知识和认识之外），——这种三元的形式，整个体系在它的一切表述中都说了出来，就像首先在《知识学》里那样。

en: The first two parts, or the opposition, is contained in its first two fundamental propositions, the first of which, I = I, is nothing but the formal identity, the infinity that has a finitude against itself, precisely because it necessarily has a second one, absolute for it, not cognisable out of I = I, outside and after itself; this second act is supposed to be conditioned as regards its matter, it is an acting in relation to another acting; but Doctrine of Science, S. 18 f.216): the condition under which the opposite of the I would be posited can by no means result from I = I, since the form of counter-positing will be so little contained in the form of positing that it is rather itself opposed to it.

That positing as well as counter-positing are both an acting of the I itself — with this identity, which is the same one that was found in the former subject, the simple substance of the soul, as the common receptacle for many opposed activities, so little is served that it is rather the most formal thing and that which this philosophy must most highly disdain.

And the beginning with the opposition is partly a preliminary, problematic philosophising, which busies itself with things that are nothing, with empty abstractions, and only in the subsequent synthesis procures reality for them — as Fichte admits that this pure I and not-I outside and before the productive imagination has a subsistence for thinking only through an illusion of the imagination —, partly this problematic philosophising, which sets the infinite, thinking, absolutely over against counter-positing, the material, and postulates and empirically takes up the manifold material or the counter-positing in addition to the first, since such a counter-positing is found in the consciousness of everyone, does not [resolve] itself in true identity.
zh: 最初的两个部分，或者说对立，包含在它的最初两个根本命题里，其中第一个，即“我 = 我”，无非是形式同一性，即自身对面有一个有限性的无限性，正因为它必然还在自身之外和自身之后有一个第二个命题，这第二个命题对它来说是绝对的、不能从“我 = 我”认识出来；这第二个行动就质料而言应当是有条件的，它是一种与另一个行动相关联的行动；但《知识学》，S. 18 f.216)：那个据以设定我的对立面的条件，根本不可能从“我 = 我”里得出，因为设立对立的形式在设定的形式里包含得如此之少，以至于它反倒与设定的形式本身相对立。
至于设定和设立对立两者都是我这个我自身的行动——靠这种同一性，也就是从前那个主体、即灵魂的单纯实体作为各种对立活动的共同容器时所显出的那同一种同一性，是帮不了什么忙的，它反倒是最形式的东西，是这种哲学必须最极端地蔑视的东西。

而以对立为开端，一部分是一种暂时的、成问题的哲学活动，它跟那些什么也不是的东西、跟空洞的抽象打交道，并且只有在随后的综合中才给它们弄出实在性——正如费希特承认的那样，这个纯粹的我与非我，在生产性的想象力之外、之前，只是通过想象力的一种欺骗，才对思维有一种持存——；另一部分，这种成问题的哲学活动把无限者、思维，与设立对立、与材料绝对地对立起来，并且把杂多的材料或设立对立公设地加到那最初的东西上、经验地接纳下来，因为据说在每个人的意识里都找得到这样一种设立对立，——它并不在真正的同一性中[消解]自身。

en: The third fundamental proposition is the relating in the indicated doubled respect: in the one respect, that of formal knowing and of finite relating through causal connection, which is wholly in difference and in division; in the other respect, that of faith, through which the absolute identity is outside cognition; but both sides of the relation, the form as knowing and the matter of faith, can absolutely not become one.

The singling out of the one member of the opposition, namely infinity, the one-sided reflection on the first fundamental proposition, constitutes idealism, but no differently than the commonest abstraction is an idealism, as negation of particularity, positively formal identity.
zh: 第三个根本命题就是上述双重意义上的关联：一重是形式的知识、以及通过因果联系而来的有限关联，它完全处在差别和划分之中；另一重是就信仰而言的关联，通过信仰，绝对同一性处在认识之外；不过关联的双方，即作为知识的形式和信仰的质料，根本不可能成为一体。
把对立的一个环节，也就是无限性，单独提出来，对第一个根本命题作片面的反思，这就构成了观念论，但这与最平庸的抽象也是一种观念论并无不同：这种抽象作为对特殊性的否定，是肯定的形式同一性。

en: By reason of this form of triplicity, in which knowing is in difference while the non-different is only either infinity, formal identity, or beyond cognition, the Fichtean system does not step out of the principle of general common sense; and after the false prejudice had spread that it is not the system of ordinary common sense but a speculative system, it gives itself, as is only fair, all pains to root out this prejudice in more recent presentations.

Nothing is clearer than that Jacobi has misunderstood this system, if in the Letter to Fichte he believes a philosophy of one piece, a true system of reason, to be brought forth in the Fichtean way, indeed to be possible in the Fichtean way alone.

Jacobi sets over against the Fichtean philosophy that he understands by the true something that is before and outside knowledge.217) But herein the Fichtean philosophy fully agrees with the Jacobian; for it, the absolute is only in faith, not in cognition.

Fichte sins as little against the majesty of the place where the true is outside cognition, as Jacobi says (Preface to the Letter, p. VIII)218), — he is as little willing to enclose it within the domain of science, that rather for him absolute identity is simply outside knowledge, that knowledge is only, as Jacobi demands, formal and in difference, that I cannot be equal to I, that the absolute cannot be thought, but only subject and object, one after the other, one determining the other, can be thought, and both only in the causal connection.
On this point, that one cannot think the absolute identity of thinking and being, Spinoza says in Principiorum Philosophiae Cartesii Pars I, Prop.

VI, schol.: "There are some who deny that they have any idea of God (that is, as Spinoza defines God, of the being in whose idea existence is necessary, or whose idea and being are one), and whom they nevertheless, as they themselves say, worship and love."

And although you set before their eyes the definition of God and God's attributes, you will nevertheless accomplish nothing: by Hercules, no more than if you tried to teach a man blind from birth the differences of colours as we see them.
But unless we want to regard them as a new kind of animal, namely a middle sort between human beings and beasts, we must care little for their words.219)
zh: 由于这种三重性的形式——在其中，知识处于差别之中，而非差别的东西却要么只是无限性、形式的同一性，要么在认识之外——，费希特体系并没有走出一般常识的原则，而在那种错误的成见蔓延开来、以为它不是平庸常识的体系而是一个思辨体系之后，它也就理所当然地费尽力气，要在较新的阐述中把这种成见连根拔掉。
再清楚不过的是：雅可比误解了这个体系，因为他在《致费希特的信》里以为，一个整块铸成的哲学、一个真正的理性体系，是按费希特的方式产生出来的，甚至以为它只有按费希特的方式才可能。
雅可比提出来与费希特哲学相对的是：他所谓真的东西，是某种在知识之前、在知识之外的东西。217) 但费希特哲学在这一点上完全与雅可比哲学一致；在它看来，绝对者只在信仰中，而不在认识中。
费希特——正如雅可比（《书信》序言，S. VIII）所说——对那个真在认识之外的处所的尊严，冒犯得同样少218)，——他也同样不愿把这个处所关进科学的领域，以致在他看来，绝对同一性干脆就在知识之外，知识则像雅可比所要求的那样只是形式性的、处在差别之中，以致我不能等于我，以致绝对者不能被思维，而只有主体和客体、一个接一个、一个规定另一个，才能被思维，而且两者都只能在因果联系中被思维。
关于这一点，即人们不能思维思维与存在的绝对同一性，斯宾诺莎在 Principiorum Philosophiae Cartesii Pars I, Prop. 中说。
VI, schol.: “Quidam sunt, qui negant, se ullam Dei（也就是说，按斯宾诺莎对神的定义，即那个本质：其观念中必然包含存在，或者说其观念与存在是一回事）ideam habere, quem tamen, ut ipsi aiunt, colunt et amant.”（“有些人否认自己拥有关于神的任何观念，可是他们又说，他们敬拜他、爱他。”）

“Et quamvis ipsis Dei definitionem Deique attributa ob oculos ponas, nihil tamen proficies: non hercle magis quam si virum a nativitate coecum colorum differentias, prout ipsos videmus, docere moliaris.”（“即使你把神的定义和神的属性摆在他们眼前，你也仍然一事无成：赫拉克勒斯作证，这并不比你想教一个天生失明的人认识我们所看到的那些颜色差别更有成效。”）

“Verum, nisi eos, tanquam pro novo animalium genere, medio silicet inter homines et bruta, habere velimus, eorum verba parum curare debemus.219)”（“但是，如果我们不想把他们当作一个新的动物种类、即介于人和野兽之间的一种中间物来看待，那么我们就不得不很少在意他们的话。”219)）

en: Why the Jacobian philosophy so greatly abhors the nihilism that it finds in the Fichtean has been shown above; but as concerns the Fichtean system itself in this matter, the task of nihilism does indeed lie in pure thinking; but pure thinking is not capable of attaining it, because this pure thinking absolutely remains on only one side and therefore this infinite possibility has an infinite actuality over against it and at the same time with it.

And so the I is affected, absolutely out into infinity, by a not-I, as it must be, since infinity, thinking, which is only one member of the opposition, is supposed to be posited as being in itself; but for that reason its correlatum can absolutely not be annihilated, but springs forth with invincible elasticity, for both are forged together by the highest fate with diamond chains.
But the first thing in philosophy is to cognize the absolute nothing, to which the Fichtean philosophy brings it as little as the Jacobian abhors it for that reason.
By contrast, both are in the nothing opposed to philosophy; the finite, appearance, has absolute reality for both; the absolute and eternal is for both the nothing for cognition.

Jacobi reproaches the Kantian system with being a mixture of idealism and empiricism; of these two ingredients it is not empiricism that his reproach hits, but the idealistic element, or the side of infinity.

Although it cannot attain the perfection of the true nothing, it is even so the unbearable for him, because it threatens the absoluteness of the empirical and in it lies the demand for the annihilation of the opposition.
zh: 雅可比哲学为什么如此厌恶它在费希特那里发现的虚无主义，前面已经指出；但就费希特体系本身在这件事上的情形而言，虚无主义的任务确实就在纯粹思维之中；只是纯粹思维没有能力达到这一步，因为这种纯粹思维根本只停在一边，所以这个无限的可能性有一个无限的现实性既在它对面、又同它在一起。
于是，我根本就是被一个非我刺激着，一直进入无限性之中，这必然如此，因为无限性，即思维，只是对立的一个环节，却应当被设定为自在存在着的；但正因如此，它的 correlatum 根本不能被消灭，反而带着不可克服的弹性跳出来，因为两者已被最高的命运用金刚石的链条锻接在一起。
但哲学的第一件事是认识绝对的无，费希特哲学很少做到这一步，雅可比哲学也正因此对它厌恶至极。
与此相反，两者都处在与哲学相对的无之中；有限的东西、现象，对两者来说都有绝对的实在性；绝对者和永恒者，对两者来说都是认识的无。
雅可比指责康德体系是观念论和经验主义的混合物；在这两种成分里，他的指责所击中的不是经验主义，而是观念论的东西，或者说无限性这一面。
尽管它得不到真正的无的那种完满，它单是这样就已经让他受不了，因为它危及经验的东西的绝对性，而它里面就包含着消灭对立的要求。

en: Jacobi says: "God is and is outside me, a living being existing for itself, or I am God.

There is no third."220) There is a third, says philosophy by contrast, and it is philosophy through this, that there is a third — in that it predicates of God not merely a being but also thinking, that is, I, and cognizes him as the absolute identity of both, recognizes no outside for God and therefore just as little cognizes him as such a being existing for itself, which would be determined by an outside-of-it, that is, outside which there would still be another subsistence, but recognizes no subsistence and nothing at all outside God, and thus absolutely annihilates in the absolute middle the either-or, which is a principle of all formal logic and of the understanding that renounces reason.

That Jacobian basic thought, in which his philosophy expresses itself completely, of which one could at the same time also show that Jacobi contradicts it not only on the preceding page, where he expresses it, in that he says that he asserts: man finds God because he can find himself only in God, but also in a hundred other places, where he calls reason divine and so on — if it had not been sufficiently shown elsewhere that such beginnings of philosophical thoughts are supposed to be absolutely only something ingenious, nothing philosophical, and [he,] where he finds these notions of his taken up philosophically by others and seriously presented as a truth for knowing, not only scents atheism and so on but dogmatically asserts it, and, where he himself goes beyond having notions and comes to thinking, is in an absolute dualism —, this Jacobian fundamental proposition is just as much a Fichtean principle.
The moral world order, which is in faith, is absolutely also outside the I; the I comes into it, or it comes only into the I, obtains reality only for the I in infinite progress.

For the I, things absolutely cannot become what they are supposed to be, because precisely thereby the not-I would cease to be and would become I, I = I as truly absolute identity without a second fundamental proposition would be, the I would sublate something that it has itself posited and would itself cease to be I.
Thus in the system of this knowing there is as little to be thought of a coming out of dualism as Jacobi can only demand it.

The non-dualistic reality is in faith, and in the Fichtean system there is just as little that third which is truly the first and only, as the non-dualistic negativity, infinity, can be purely the nothing; it is supposed to be pure, but does not become so, but is itself again fixed and thereby absolute subjectivity.

Jacobi, who, in that he reflected on the one side of the opposition, infinity, formal identity, opined that this nihilism of transcendental philosophy wanted to tear his heart out of his bosom, had only to reflect on the other side of the opposition, which is just as absolutely present, where he could find all the affections and states of mind, all revealed and believed empirical [content], before as after.
zh: 雅可比说：“上帝存在，并且在我之外，是一个活生生的、自为地存在着的本质，或者我就是上帝。

“没有第三个。”220) 哲学则说，有第三个，而且哲学之所以是哲学，就在于有第三个——因为它对上帝不仅断言一个存在，而且断言思维，即断言我，并且把他认作两者的绝对同一性，不承认在上帝之外还有什么“外”，因而同样不把他认作这样一个自为地存在着的本质——这个本质会由一个在它之外的东西来规定，也就是说，在它之外还会有别的存在——，反倒不承认在上帝之外还有什么存在、还有什么东西，于是在绝对的中点上根本消灭了那种非此即彼，而非此即彼是一切形式逻辑的原则，也是那个放弃理性的知性的原则。

那个雅可比的基本思想——他的哲学在其中完整地说了出来，关于它，人们同时还可以指出：雅可比不只是在前面那一页、在他把它说出来的地方与它相矛盾，他说他主张，人找到上帝，是因为人只有在上帝中才能找到自己，而且在上百个别的地方也与它相矛盾，在那些地方他称理性为神性的等等——，如果不是别处已经充分地表明，这类哲学思想的萌芽根本只应当是某种机智的东西、而不是哲学的东西，而且他在发现自己的这些念头被别人从哲学上接过去、并被认真当作一种为知识而设的真理来陈述时，就不只是嗅到无神论等等，而是独断地断言它，并且在他自己超出拥有念头、达到思维的地方，就处在一种绝对的二元论之中——，那么这个雅可比的根本命题就同样也是费希特的原则。
那在信仰中的道德世界秩序，根本也在我之外；我进入它，或者说它只进入我之中，只在无限的进展中获得对我的实在性。
对我来说，事物根本不可能成为它们应当成为的样子，因为这样一来非我就会不再存在、就会变成我，就会是作为真正绝对的同一性、不需要第二个根本命题的“我 = 我”；我就会扬弃某种它自己设定起来的东西，它自己也就不再是我。
因此，在这个知识的体系里，要设想走出二元论，和雅可比所能要求的同样少。
非二元论的实在性在信仰之中，而在费希特体系里，既没有那个真正是第一位和唯一者的第三者，非二元论的否定性、无限性也同样不能纯粹地是无；它应当是纯粹的，却做不到，反而它自身又被固定下来，并因此成了绝对的主观性。
雅可比把反思对准对立的一面，即无限性、形式的同一性，就以为先验哲学的这种虚无主义要把他胸中的心掏出来，其实他只要把反思对准对立的另一面——这一面同样绝对地存在——，就能在那里找到他从前和现在都能找到的一切感受和心情状态、一切被启示出来的和被信仰的经验的东西。

en: Theoretical science of this idealism now means nothing other than the producing of that opposition of infinity and finitude, on the one side of the abstraction of pure knowing and thinking, as knowing and thinking, and on the other side of the abstraction of not-knowing and not-thinking, or of the not-I.
Both are posited only in and for knowing, the one abstraction and emptiness as the other.
The empirical side in the theoretical is in general the abstraction of the manifold, a not-I.
Since the real itself is thus posited wholly formally or ideally, the whole framework of this theoretical idealism is nothing but the construction of the logical forms that abstract from all content.

The scientific path that this formal or logical idealism takes in its transition to reality, which it calls a deduction of the same, has been indicated above; its own content is the relative identities between empty thinking and the abstraction of the manifold, which three members therefore themselves fall wholly within empty knowing.
We have now to consider the integration of this emptiness according to its content.
In theoretical idealism the empirical is an abstraction, but in the practical it appears as true empirical, visible and palpable reality.

Nature, which there was only a not-I, a merely negative, determined as the opposed in general, here steps out of the abstraction of knowing into the wealth of its reality and into the splendour of its fullness of life — namely, to be a sour and sweet and bitter, a blue and red.
zh: 这种观念论的理论科学，现在无非意味着把无限性与有限性的那个对立产生出来：一面是纯粹知识和纯粹思维的抽象，作为知识和思维，另一面是不知和不思的抽象，或者说非我的抽象。
两者都只在知识之中、只为知识而设定，一个和另一个一样是抽象和空洞。
在理论的东西里，经验的一面一般就是杂多的抽象，是一个非我。
既然实在物本身就这样被完全形式地或观念地设定起来，那么这个理论观念论的整个骨架，就无非是对那些从一切内容中抽离出来的逻辑形式的建构。
这个形式的或逻辑的观念论在向实在性过渡时（它把这一过渡称为对实在性的演绎）所走的科学道路，前面已经指出；它自己的内容，是空洞的思维与杂多的抽象之间那些相对的同一性，而这三个环节因此本身完全落在空洞的知识之内。
我们现在要来考察这种空洞按其内容而言的整合。
在理论观念论里，经验的东西是一种抽象，而在实践观念论里，它却作为真正的、经验的、看得见摸得着的实在性出现。
自然在那里只是一个非我，一个单纯否定的东西，被规定为一般意义上的对立面，而在这里，它从知识的抽象中走出来，进入自己实在性的丰富和生命充实的壮丽之中——也就是说，它是酸的、甜的和苦的，是蓝的和红的。

en: In the Jacobian philosophy this integration is already present immediately, through its original empiricism and the non-abstracted particularity of the subject.

In the Kantian philosophy the particular, of which the universality of reason stands in need — which, insofar as it has this need, is called practical reason — is likewise assumed in an empirical and unconcerned way; the presence of the particular, of the inclinations and passions, of the pathological in general, which is to be combated by reason, [and] nature, which is to be worked upon by reason and subjected to the purpose of reason — for it is not yet realized in it — are taken as given, and the content of the purpose of reason itself, the highest good, happiness according to merit — and everyone is to have merit, hence universal happiness in general — is, as to that in which this happiness consists, likewise empirically presupposed.

The Fichtean integration through reality takes place a priori, namely through faith, which is the principle of the transition from lack into fullness in general, or the pure form of the transformation of the minus into the plus and of the linking of both in reciprocal action upon each other — but also only the form, for the matter itself, from which in the minus of ideality abstraction has been made, is, as is necessary, just as empirical and without totality as in the preceding systems.
zh: 在雅可比哲学里，这种整合通过它原本的经验主义和主体那种没有被抽象掉的特殊性，已经直接现成地存在着。

在康德哲学里，特殊东西——理性的普遍性需要它，而理性的普遍性既然有这种需要，就叫作实践理性——同样是以经验的、满不在乎的方式被假定的；特殊东西、爱好和激情、要由理性去斗争的一般病理东西的现成存在，以及那种要由理性去加工、并使之服从理性目的的自然——因为理性目的现在还没有在自然里实现——，都被当作给定的，而理性目的本身的内容，即至善、按功绩而来的幸福——而且每个人都该有功绩，所以也就是一般的普遍幸福——，也同样按这幸福究竟在于什么而经验地被预先假定了。
费希特式的通过实在性的整合是 a priori（先验地）发生的，也就是说，是通过信仰发生的：信仰是一般从匮乏向充实过渡的原则，或者说，是把减号变为加号、并把两者在彼此交互作用中联结起来的纯粹形式——但也只是形式，因为那材料本身，也就是在观念性的减号里被抽掉的那个材料，正如必然的那样，和前面那些体系里一样，同样是经验的、同样没有总体性。

en: The fundamental principle that governs everything, namely that of the integration of the ideal through the real, of the concurrence of empty thinking or of reason with the sense-world that stands over against it as nature here appears, consists in this, that absolutely the one is not what the other is, and that in all linking of them no true identity comes out.
True identity and eternity is, as for knowledge in the beyond of faith, so in the practical and the real likewise beyond, namely in infinite progress.
As there empty thinking as pure knowledge or theoretical reason, so here it is absolute as pure will or as practical reason, and so too its opposite is an absolute empirical sense-world.
The practical relative identities, which Kant has elaborated less, will emerge in their various branches.
zh: 那个支配一切的根本原则，即观念物通过实在物而得到整合、空洞的思维或理性与那个——照自然在这里显现的样子——与它相对而立的感性世界相会合的原则，就在于：一个绝对不是另一个所是的东西，并且在对两者的任何联结中都得不出真的同一性。
真正的同一性和永恒，正如对知识来说在信仰的彼岸，在实践的东西和实在物里同样也在彼岸，也就是说，在无限的进展里。
正如在那里，空洞的思维作为纯粹知识或理论理性是绝对的，在这里，它作为纯粹意志或实践理性也是绝对的，而它的对立面同样是一个绝对的经验的感性世界。
康德较少加以展开的那些实践的相对同一性，将在它们的不同分支里显示出来。

en: But the first thing in the integration, above all, must be this: to reintroduce the reality of both members of the opposition against one another, or to sublate the theoretical abstraction and to constitute faith according to its product.

The theoretical consists in ideality, or in the reflection on infinity, which is both infinity as such — empty knowing, pure thinking — and absolute opposition 0 = + 1 - 1, and each determines that the one is not what the other is.

The one is only insofar as the other enters, and as the other enters, it is not; the reality of infinity or of empty thinking consists in the + 1 - 1, and the persistence of this opposition gives the content of idealism or the logical forms; at the same time, however, they are ideal = 0, and their true truth is in infinity, or in this, that they are nothing.
zh: 但在这种整合中，首要之事尤其必须是：把对立两项各自的实在性重新相互引进来，或者说，扬弃理论的抽象，并按信仰的产物来确立信仰。
理论的东西在于观念性，或者说在于对无限性的反思——这种无限性既是作为这样的无限性、即空洞的知识、纯粹的思维，又是绝对的对立 0 = + 1 - 1，并且每一方都规定：一方不是另一方所是的东西。
一方只有在另一方进入时才存在，而随着另一方的进入，它就不是；无限性、或者说空洞思维的实在性就在于那个 + 1 - 1，而这种对立的持存就给出观念论的内容、即那些逻辑形式；但同时它们又是观念的 = 0，而它们真正的真理在无限性中，或者说就在于它们什么都不是。

en: This ideality is now to be sublated in the practical; the + 1 and - 1 are not to be equal to zero, and the reality that they receive is that infinity, empty thinking, which is the middle + 1, 0, - 1 in which they sink, steps out of the middle to the side, and over against it the world of sense, the realm of finite existence.
This constituting of both as realities is called the pure act of will, which decrees the nothing of the + 1 and - 1 to be an absolute something.
Into this fall all those popularities: that you are there for action, and that your action determines your value, the absoluteness of practical reason, absolute freedom, etc.
zh: 这种观念性现在要在实践的东西中被扬弃；+ 1 和 - 1 不应当等于零，而它们所获得的实在性就在于：无限性、即空洞的思维——它是那个中间 + 1, 0, - 1，它们在其中沉没——从中间移到一边去，而与之相对的是感性世界、即有限存在的王国。
把两者确立为实在性，这叫做纯粹的意志行动，它把 + 1 和 - 1 的无裁定为绝对的某物。
所有那些通俗论调都落进这里面：你是为行动而在的，你的行动规定你的价值，实践理性的绝对性，绝对自由，等等。

en: But after these nothings of absolute opposition have been absolutely decreed to be realities, everything that follows hangs formaliter on faith, which is the expression of the demanded identity of both.

But it is wholly formal for the cognition and construction of the practical, for it expresses nothing but this demand, the pure line of a thread that can absolutely have no fulfilment, no depth, nor length and breadth, and admits only relative identities that still have the demand behind them.
Subjectivity, I, pure will, opposed to objectivity, is in absolute opposition, and the task of identity and integration is absolutely not to be solved.
zh: 但既然绝对对立的这些无被绝对地裁定为实在性，那么后面的一切就 formaliter（形式上）系于信仰，而信仰就是两者被要求的同一性的表达。
但对实践东西的认识和建构来说，它完全是形式性的，因为它所表达的不过是这一要求，即一根线的纯粹线条，而这根线绝对不可能有任何充实、任何深度，也没有长度和宽度，它只容许那些背后始终还有这一要求的相对同一性。
主体性，即我、纯粹意志，与客观性相对立，它处在绝对的对立之中，而同一性和整合的任务是绝对无法解决的。

en: The pure will is to become real through acting; the reality that springs to it through acting is to come from it, to be its own: it must therefore first of all be present in it ideally, as the intention and purpose of the subject.

The I is to project the concept absolutely freely out of the absolute plenitude of power of itself as intelligence, and the will is to be affected by no other reality that it might make its purpose as given from somewhere, but as pure will is to have only the purpose freely projected by it.
In that the human being determines himself to act, there arises for him the concept of a future thing that will follow from his acting, and this is the formal element of the concept of purpose.
But the will is pure identity without all content, and pure only insofar as it is something thoroughly formal, contentless.

It is in itself impossible that its concept of purpose should have a content out of it, and there remains thoroughly nothing but this formal idealism of faith, which posits the empty subjective of the purpose just as emptily objective, without being able or permitted in the least to give the purpose an inner reality or content; for otherwise the pure will is no longer the determining element.

And there remains nothing but the hollow declamation that the law must be fulfilled for the law's sake, duty for duty's sake, and how the I raises itself above the sensible and the supersensible, hovers over the ruins of the worlds, etc.
zh: 纯粹意志应当通过行动而成为实在的；通过行动向它产生的实在性应当来自它、是它自己的东西：所以它必须首先在它里面以观念的方式现成存在，作为主体的意图和目的。
我要作为智性，从它自身的绝对全能出发、绝对自由地构想出概念，而意志不应被任何别的实在性所触动，不应把这种实在性当作从某处给予的东西立为目的，而是作为纯粹意志只应有它自由构想出来的目的。
当人规定自己去行动时，他那里就产生出一个将来之物的概念，这个将来之物将从他的行动中产生出来，而这就是目的概念的形式东西。
但意志是没有一切内容的纯粹同一性，并且只有就它是一种彻底形式性的、无内容的东西而言，才是纯粹的。
自在说来，它的目的概念要从它那里得到一个内容，这是不可能的，于是完全只剩下信仰的这种形式的观念论，它把目的中空洞的主观东西同样空洞地设定为客观的，却丝毫不能、也不许给目的一种内在的实在性或内容；因为否则纯粹意志就不再是规定者了。
于是剩下的无非是空洞的宣言：法则必须为法则的缘故、义务必须为义务的缘故而被履行，以及我如何把自己抬高到感性东西和超感性东西之上、如何在诸世界的废墟之上翱翔等等。

en: This sublime hollowness and uniquely consistent emptiness must then concede so much as to take reality into account, and if the content is to be set up as a system of duties and laws for scientific purposes, then either the ideal reality or the content of the laws, duties and virtues is empirically scraped together, as Kant especially does, or it is deduced from a finite starting point, running on through finitudes, as Fichte arbitrarily begins from a rational being, and one that has no body, etc.

But in whatever way the system is set up, there arises, because reality can only be a manifoldness, since it remains in opposition to ideality, a multitude of duties, laws or virtues, and indeed an infinite one, which for that very reason attain neither to totality nor to the external completeness of a system, and also necessarily contradict themselves in their determinacy and are capable of no limitation by one another or of any preference and subordination among one another, because each is posited into the ideal form and thus appears with the pretension of absoluteness.
The Fichtean and Kantian moral sciences are the empirical proofs of this.
zh: 这种崇高的空洞和唯一一贯到底的虚空，于是必须让步到如此地步，竟要顾及实在性；而如果为了科学的目的要把内容建立为一个义务和法则的体系，那么要么像康德尤其做的那样，把观念的实在性或者法则、义务和德性的内容经验地抓拢来，要么从一个有限的出发点出发、沿着一个又一个有限物演绎下去，就像费希特任意地从一种理性存在者、而且是这样一个没有肉体的存在者等等出发那样。
但不管这个体系以什么方式建立起来，由于实在性只能是一种杂多——因为它始终处在与观念性的对立之中——，都会产生出一批义务、法则或德性，而且是无限多的一批；这些东西正因如此既达不到总体性，也达不到一个体系的外在完整性，而且它们在自己的规定性里必然相互矛盾，既不能由彼此来限制，也不能有彼此之间的优先和从属，因为每一个都被置入了观念的形式，因而带着绝对性的僭称出场。
费希特和康德的道德科学就是这一点的经验证据。

en: Thus on one side pure reason stands integrated.
If it asserts itself as pure will, it is in its assertion a hollow declamation.

If it gives itself a content, it must take it up empirically, and if it has given it the form of practical ideality or made it into law and duty, then an absolute, all science sublating, totality-less conflict of this content is posited.
zh: 这样，纯粹理性就作为被整合的东西站在一边。
如果它作为纯粹意志坚持自己，那么它在自己的坚持里就是一场空洞的宣言。
如果它给自己一个内容，它就必须经验地接受这个内容；而如果它已经给了这个内容以实践观念性的形式，或者已经把它变成了法则和义务，那么被设定起来的就是这个内容的一种绝对的、扬弃一切科学的、没有总体性的冲突。

en: But on the other side stands nature, made absolute and made into empirical reality by the pure act of will.
What the idealistic side annihilated must, because that side itself absolutely decrees itself, likewise come forth again.
If empirical reality or the sensible world were not there in the whole strength of its opposition, then the I would cease to be I; it could not act, its high vocation would be gone.

The supersensible world is only the flight from the sensible one; if there is nothing more to flee from, then flight and freedom and the supersensible world are no longer posited, and this empirical reality is just as much in itself as the I.
At the same time, the relation that it receives in the act of will determines the manner in which it must be.

Namely, the essence of the I consists in acting: absolute empty thinking is to posit itself; it is not posited, no being belongs to it; but the objective world is its being, and it can attain its true essence only by annihilating this being, and nature is thus determined as mere sensible world, as something to be annihilated, and must be cognised as such.

If, on the other hand, the I cognises itself as existing just as it does the objective, then it cognises itself as absolutely dependent on the world and caught up in an absolute necessity; it must cognise itself only as negation of the sensible world, and the sensible world therefore as something to be negated or as something absolutely bad.
zh: 但在另一面，则是通过纯粹意志行为而被弄得绝对、并被造成经验的实在性的自然。
观念论的一面所消灭的东西，因为这一面自己把自己绝对地颁布出来，所以同样必须重新出现。
如果经验的实在性或感性世界不是处在它对立的全部强度之中，那么我就停止其为我了；它就不能行动，它崇高的使命也就完了。
超感性世界只是对感性世界的逃避；如果不再有什么东西可供逃避，那么逃避、自由和超感性世界就不再被设定，而这经验的实在性和我一样是自在的。
同时，它在意志行为中所获得的那种关系，也规定着它必须如何存在的方式。
这就是说，我的本质在于行动：绝对空洞的思维应当把自己设定起来；它没有被设定，没有任何存在归于它；但客观世界就是它的存在，而它只有消灭这个存在才能达到自己真正的本质，于是自然就被规定为单纯的感性世界、规定为要被消灭的东西，并且必须作为这样的东西被认识。
反之，如果我像认识客观的东西那样把自己也认识为存在着的，那么我就把自己认识为绝对依赖于世界、并陷在一种绝对的必然性之中；我必须只把自己认识为感性世界的否定，因而也把感性世界认识为要被否定的东西、或某种绝对坏的东西。

en: That first cognition of the world as something real, which precedes the pure act of will, in which the world again receives absolute reality, but such a one as must be annihilated, that is, the worst thinkable, is presented by the first act in the Vocation of Man221), in which the I cognises itself as 'an utterance, determined by the universe, of a natural force determined by itself', and [cognises] that nature acts in it, that it stands under the eternal laws of nature and a strict necessity, that it will be the most calming thing to subject its wishes to nature, since its being is wholly subject to it.
But his wishes 'resist this rational thought.
Why should he conceal from himself the sadness, the loathing, the horror that seize his inmost being at such a conclusion?'
zh: 那种把世界认作实在物的最初认识——它先于纯粹意志行为，而在纯粹意志行为中世界又重新获得绝对的实在性，不过是一种必须被消灭的实在性，也就是可以想象的最坏的实在性——，是由《人的使命》221)里的第一幕呈现出来的：在其中我把自己认识为“一种由宇宙规定的、由自身规定的自然力量的表露”，并且认识到自然在我之中行动、我处在自然的永恒法则和一种严格的必然性之下、最令人安宁的将是把自己的愿望交给自然，因为我的存在完全服从于自然。
可是他的愿望却‘抗拒这个理性的思想。
他为什么要把在这样一个结论面前攫住他内心深处的忧伤、厌恶、恐惧对自己隐瞒起来呢？’

en: This monstrous arrogance, this madness of the conceit of this I, to be horrified at the thought, to loathe it, to become sad over the fact that it is one with the universe, that the eternal nature acts in it — to loathe its resolve to submit itself to the eternal laws of nature and their holy and strict necessity, to be horrified at that and to become sad over it, to fall into despair if it is not free, free from the eternal laws of nature and their strict necessity, to believe itself made unspeakably wretched by that obedience — already presupposes in general a most common view of nature, stripped of all reason, and of the relation of singleness to it, a view to which the absolute identity of subject and object is utterly foreign and whose principle is absolute non-identity, which therefore can also conceive nature simply only under the form of absolute opposition, thus as pure object, of which it is only possible to be dependent or to make it dependent on oneself, which finds itself in general in the causal connection — a view of nature as a thing in which (Vocation of Man, p. 106) are found 'differences of green, sweet, red, smooth, bitter, fragrance, rough, violin sound, bad smell, sound of trumpet'.

What, besides such qualities — and which other teleological qualities Fichte also knows of nature, we shall see below — may the laws of nature further be, of which it is often repeated that no created spirit penetrates into their interior?

As if they were something entirely different from rational laws — laws that the I is ashamed to submit itself to, to obey which would make it unspeakably wretched, to be subjected to which would drive it to despair?
zh: 这种骇人的傲慢，这种这个我的自负的疯狂，竟对那个思想感到恐惧、厌恶它、为它和宇宙是一体、为永恒的自然在它之中行动而变得忧伤，——竟厌恶自己服从自然的永恒法则及其神圣而严格的必然性的决心，对此感到恐惧和忧伤，在它不自由、即不摆脱自然的永恒法则、不摆脱它那严格的必然性时陷入绝望，相信自己会由于那种服从变得不可言说地悲惨，——这种傲慢本身就已经预设了一种被剥夺了一切理性的、最平庸的自然观，以及对单一性同自然的关系的看法，这种看法对主体与客体的绝对同一性完全陌生，其原则是绝对的非同一性，因此它也只能把自然仅仅在绝对对立的形式下、也就是作为纯粹客体以概念把握，对这个客体只可能要么依赖于它、要么使它依赖于自己，它总的来说处在因果联系之中，——以及一种把自然看作一个物的看法，其中（《人的使命》，S. 106）有“绿、甜、红、滑、苦、香、粗糙、小提琴声、臭味、喇叭声的区别”。
除了这样的性质之外——费希特究竟还从自然那里知道哪些别的目的论性质，我们下面会看到——，自然的法则还可能是什么呢，而关于这些法则人们又常常反复说，任何被创造的精神都钻不进自然的内部？
就好像它们与理性的法则完全是两回事似的——这些法则，我羞于服从它们，服从它们会使我变得不可言说地悲惨，受它们支配则会把我逼向绝望？

en: After the I, in the second act of his Vocation, thinks to lose through knowledge, as we saw above, this nature at which he is so horrified, and over its loss again becomes just as inconsolable and falls into despair as over its being, he then produces it for himself through his vocation, acting and the pure act of will — as a nature that must be annihilated.

This intuition of nature as something that is nothing in itself but pure appearance, and thus has neither truth nor beauty in itself, thus grounds a teleology of nature and a physicotheology that is directly opposed in content to the older one, but in form is grounded in the same principle.

For that older teleology related nature in the individual to purposes that [are] outside this individual, so that each would be posited only for the sake of another — but on the whole it would form a system that indeed also had the source of its life outside itself, but would be a reflection of eternal beauty and reason, and would bear in itself the highest and most blessed truth, the perfect law of the highest wisdom.

Fichte's teleology likewise presents that which appears as nature as something existing for the sake of another, namely in order to form a sphere and free room for free beings and in order to be able to become ruins over which they would raise themselves and so attain their vocation.

This common teleological principle, that nature is nothing in itself but only in relation to another, something absolutely unholy and dead, Fichte's philosophy has in common with all teleology, especially that of eudaimonism; but in what nature is through and for the other, Fichte's teleology is opposed to the others.
zh: 在我由于知识——正如我们上面看到的——以为失去了这个令我如此恐惧的自然，并且为失去它又变得和它为存在时一样地无可安慰、陷入绝望之后，我就通过自己的使命、即行动和纯粹意志行为，把它重新产生出来——作为一种必须被消灭的自然。
这种把自然直观为某种并非自在之物、而只是纯粹现象、因而自身既没有真理也没有美的东西的直观，于是奠定了一种自然的目的论和一种物理神学，后者在内容上与更早的那种目的论直接对立，但在形式上却建立在同一个原则之上。
因为那种更早的目的论把自然在个别的东西上关联到一些在这个个别的东西之外的合目的性，以致每一个都只是为着另一个的缘故而被设定，——但在整体上它却构成一个系统，这个系统虽然也把自己的生命之源放在自身之外，却是永恒的美和理性的反照，并且自身承载着最高的、最福乐的真理，即最高智慧的完美法则。
费希特的目的论同样把显现为自然的东西呈现为为着另一个的缘故而现存的东西，也就是为了给自由的存在者形成一个领域和活动空间，并且为了能够成为废墟，让自由的存在者在这些废墟之上把自己提高起来、从而达到了自己的使命。
这条普通的目的论原则，即自然自在什么也不是、而只在与另一个的关系中才是某种东西、并且是绝对不神圣的和死的东西，是费希特哲学与一切目的论、尤其是幸福论的目的论所共有的；但在自然通过另一个并为了另一个而是什么这一点上，费希特的目的论却与其他的目的论相对立。

en: As nature in physicotheology is the expression of eternal truth, so in Kantian and Fichtean moral theology it is something to be annihilated, on which the purpose of reason is eternally first to be realised, stripped of truth, bearing in itself the law of ugliness and of contrariety to reason; here the commonest litanies about evil in the world break in, whose pessimism Kant has put in the place of optimism, in that Kant, and Fichte after him, brought into philosophical form and systematically proved that which Voltaire — placing himself on precisely the standpoint of empiricism and thus quite consistently ad hominem — opposed to the optimism dragged down by sanctimoniousness into the empiricism of common life, whereby that consistency is then utterly lost and the relative truth of the empirical against empirical things is supposed to become an absolute one.

Voltaire's procedure is an example of genuine sound common sense, which this man possessed in so high a degree and of which others chatter so much in order to sell their unhealthy qualities as common sense.

Since a philosophical idea, dragged down into appearance and bound up with the principles of empiricism, immediately becomes a one-sidedness, true sound common sense sets over against it the other one-sidedness, which is likewise found in appearance, and thereby shows the untruth and ridiculousness of the first, in that for the first appeal is made to appearance and experience, while it points out the opposite in precisely this experience and appearance.
But the use and the truth of the second one-sidedness does not go further for itself, and genuine sound common sense does not expect more of it either.

School pedantry, by contrast, again makes itself ridiculous over against sound common sense in the same way, in that it takes absolutely that of which common sense made only this relative use ad hominem and seriously pours it into philosophical form.

This merit Kantian and Fichtean philosophy has acquired for itself with regard to Voltaire's argumentation, a merit of which the Germans generally boast: to cultivate a French conceit and to give it back improved, placed in its proper light, and carried out more thoroughly and made scientific, that is, to take from it precisely the relative truth that it has by the fact that universally valid truth, of which it is not capable, was to be conferred on it.
zh: 正如自然在物理神学里是永恒真理的表达，同样，它在康德和费希特的道德神学里则是要被消灭的东西，理性的目的在它上面永远只是首先要去实现的，它被剥夺了真理，自身带着丑恶和违背理性的法则；这里涌进来的是那些关于世间之恶的最平庸的连祷文，康德用它们的悲观主义取代了乐观主义，因为康德以及追随他的费希特，把伏尔泰当年针对那种被伪虔诚拖进日常生活的经验里去的乐观主义、自己站到经验的立场上、因而完全一贯地 ad hominem 地所提出的东西，弄成了哲学形式并加以系统证明，于是那种一贯性也就完全丧失了，而经验的东西针对经验的东西所具有的相对真理，竟应当成为一种绝对的真理。
伏尔泰的做法是名副其实的健全常识的一个例子，这种健全常识，这个人拥有到如此高的程度，而别人却对它喋喋不休，为的是把自己的不健全当作常识兜售出去。
由于一种哲学的观念被拖进现象里、并与经验的原则结合在一起，就立即变成一种片面性，所以真正的健全常识就把同样出现在现象里的另一种片面性同它对立起来，并由此显示出前一种的不真和可笑，因为人们为前一种援引现象和经验，而它却在正是这种经验和现象中指出了相反的东西。
但第二种片面性的运用和真理本身并不能再往前走了，名副其实的健全常识也不再向它要求更多。
相反，学院派的迂腐则又用同样的方式在健全常识面前把自己弄得可笑：它把健全常识只是相对地、ad hominem 地加以利用的东西绝对地接受下来，并且一本正经地把它灌进哲学形式里。
康德和费希特的哲学为自己在伏尔泰的论证上挣得了这份功劳，一份德意志人普遍自夸的功劳：把一种法国式的念头加以培养，然后把它改进过、放到它应有的光亮里、更彻底地加以发挥并使之科学化之后再还回去，也就是说，恰恰剥夺掉它拥有的相对真理，办法是应当把普遍有效的真理、而这是它没有能力承受的，授予给它。

en: Through the absolute subjectivity of reason and its opposition to reality, the world is now absolutely opposed to reason, and thereby [there is] absolute reasonless finitude and inorganic sensible world, which in the infinite progress is supposed to become equal to the I, that is, is and remains absolute.
Thus even physical nature shows itself as something contrary to reason (Vocation of Man, p. 221 ff.

[SW, Vol. II, p. 267 ff.]): 'It resists granting our race its sustenance, so that immortal spirits are compelled to fasten all their thinking and striving and their whole exertion on the soil that bears their nourishment. Even now

it often happens that a hostile weather destroys what years of work required and gives the diligent and careful man up to hunger and misery through no fault of his own' (though surely often also with debts) 'floods, storm winds, volcanoes, earthquakes; diseases that even in this current year carry people off in the bloom of their powers, and children whose existence passes by without fruit and consequence; still plagues and so on. But so it cannot be supposed to remain forever.'

However, this unconscious nature still has far more understanding than the manner in which the human race exists, of which 'still hordes of savages roam huge deserts, who, when they meet, festively devour one another; armies too, when they catch sight of one another, kill one another.
Thus equipped with the highest that human understanding has devised, war fleets cross the seas through storm and waves in order to kill one another.

These perverse human beings, of whom one part holds the other as slaves, though in eternal strife among themselves, nevertheless immediately enter into league with one another against the good, which already for itself is always the weaker, as soon as it lets itself be seen' — which they would not need at all, since besides the fact that the good is already for itself the weaker, the good themselves on their part also make their cause just as badly.

For in promoting the purpose of reason, for whose infallible attainment reason vouches, the good — in whose doing the goal of humanity [lies] and on whose doing is counted in the moral world order — these good people behave like simple-minded philistines: the good often have a secret self-love, blame and accuse one another; each such good person holds the improvement that he wants to make to be precisely the most important and best, and accuses the other good people, to whom his own is not so important, of betraying the good cause; and so on, as can be read more fully in the Vocation of Man222) itself.

In short, a moral sentimentality, if it only goes in the direction of the ugly and useless as otherwise sanctimoniousness goes in the direction of the good and useful, becomes the rational view of the world, and philosophy has placed itself in the common view of subjectivity, which, itself a contingency and arbitrariness, that is, an evil, also objectively beholds the evil, that is, contingency and arbitrariness, and has wholly surrendered its own elevation, as well as the elevation of its view of the world out of the view of an empirical necessity, which is one with contingency, into the view of an eternal necessity, which is one with freedom, the necessity of the wisdom existing as the course of the world — and to cognise what Plato says of the world, that the reason of God gave birth to it as a blessed god223) —.
zh: 由于理性的绝对主观性及其对实在性的对立，世界现在与理性绝对地对立起来，从而成为绝对无理性的有限性和无机的感性世界，这个世界在无限的进展中应当变得和我一样，也就是说，它是绝对的，并且始终是绝对的。
于是，物理的自然已经显示出自己是某种违背理性的东西（《人的使命》，S. 221 ff.
[SW, Bd. II, S. 267 ff.]）：‘它抗拒为我们人类提供生计，以致不朽的精神们不得不把自己的一切思虑和追求以及全部努力都固定在承载他们食物的土地上。直到现在
常常发生这样的事：一种恶劣的天气毁掉了需要多年劳作才有的东西，并且把勤勉而细心的人并非由于自己的过错’（不过大概也常常是带着债务地）‘交给饥饿和贫困；洪水、风暴、火山、地震；疾病，它们就在今年这一年里还把正值力量旺盛的人们夺走，还有孩子，他们的存在没有结果、没有后续地过去了；还有瘟疫等等。可是这样总不能永远下去。’
不过，这种无意识的自然毕竟还是比人类存在的方式有远为更多的知性，关于人类，‘至今还有一群群野蛮人在广袤的荒野里游荡，他们一旦相遇，就互相喜庆地吃掉对方；军队一旦看见对方，也会互相杀死。
就这样装备着人的知性所构想出来的最高东西，战争舰队穿过风暴和波涛横渡海洋，为的是互相残杀。
这些颠倒的人，其中一部分把另一部分当作奴隶来占有，尽管他们自己之间处在永恒的斗争中，可一旦善——善本身从来就是较弱的一方——露出身影，他们却立刻联合起来对付它’，——其实他们根本不必这样做，因为除了善本来就一直是较弱的一方之外，善人们在自己这一方面也把自己的事情做得同样糟糕。

因为，在促进理性的目的——理性为它不可错失的达成作担保——时，善人们（人类的目标就在他们的行动之中，道德世界秩序所指望的也正是他们的行动）——这些善人的举止活像些头脑简单的市侩：善人们常常有一种隐秘的自爱，互相责备、互相指控；每一个这样的善人都把自己想要作的改进恰好看成最重要、最好的，并且指控别的善人——因为那些善人并不觉得他的改进有那么重要——背叛了善的事业；等等，正如在《人的使命》222)本身里可以更详细地读到的那样。

总之，一种道德上的多愁善感，只要它只朝着丑恶和无用的方面走，就像伪虔诚平时朝着善和有用的方面走那样，它就成了理性的世界观，而哲学就把自己放进了主观性那种平庸的看法里，这种看法本身是一种偶然性和任意，也就是一种恶，于是它也在客观上看到恶，即偶然性和任意，并且完全放弃了自己的提高，以及放弃把自己的世界观从一种经验的必然性——这种必然性与偶然性是一回事——的看法提高到一种永恒的必然性——而这必然性与自由是一回事，即作为世界进程而存在的智慧的必然性——的看法，也放弃去认识柏拉图关于世界所说的那番话，即上帝的理性把它作为一个有福的神诞生出来223)。

en: Religion shares its view with this philosophy of absolute subjectivity so little that, while the latter conceives evil only as contingency and caprice of nature that is already in itself finite, religion on the contrary presents evil as a necessity of finite nature, as one with the concept of the same, but at the same time presents for this necessity an eternal, that is, not a redemption deferred into infinite progress and never to be realized, but a truly real and present redemption, and offers to nature, insofar as it is considered as finite and singular, a possible reconciliation, whose original possibility is the subjective in the original image of God, – while its objective is the actuality in His eternal incarnation, – while the identity of that possibility and this actuality is through the spirit as the being-one of the subjective with the God who has become man, and thus the world is in itself reconstructed, redeemed and sanctified in a wholly different way than that in the ideal of the moral world order the volcanoes etc. do not forever remain as they still are, than that they gradually burn out, the hurricanes become gentler, the diseases less painful, the air of the forests and swamps is improved, etc.; and because in religion the world is sanctified according to its essence, it is posited as unholy only for the limitation of cognition, empirical intuition and its own positing of ends, while perfect intuition and eternal blessedness are expressly posited beyond the limitation, the limitation which is to be immanent in the moral world order and for whose sake even the volcanoes are to burn out, the earthquakes become gentler, etc., the peoples [are to] no longer make war upon one another nor plunder one another, etc., and which is to remain absolutely.

In this philosophy, by contrast, the world is neither originally nature and divine, nor reconciled in its ethical aspect, but in itself something bad; for finitude, however, evil is after all only something contingent and capricious.

But if the physical and ethical world were in itself more than a bad world of sense, and if badness were not absolute, then the other absolute, freedom, would also fall away — that pure will which needs a world in which reason is first to be realized — and with it the whole worth of man, because this freedom only is by negating, and can only negate as long as that which it negates is.
zh: 宗教与这种绝对主体性的哲学在看法上如此少有共同之处，以至于当后者只把灾祸理解为那已经自在地是有限的自然的偶然性和任意时，宗教反倒把恶描述为有限自然的必然性，描述为与有限自然的概念合一的东西，但同时为这种必然性描述出一种永恒的、也就是并非被推移到无限进展之中并且永远无法实现的解救，而是一种真正实在的、现成的解救，并且为自然——就自然被看作有限的和单个的而言——提供一种可能的和解：这种和解的本源可能性是上帝本源形象中的主观的东西，——而它的客观的东西则是上帝在其永恒道成肉身中的现实性，——但那种可能性与这种现实性的同一性却通过精神、作为主观的东西与成为人的上帝的合而为一，于是世界自在地被重构、被解救，并且以一种完全不同的方式被神圣化，不同于在道德世界秩序的理想中火山等等并不永远保持它们现在还是的样子，不同于那些火山渐渐熄灭、飓风变得温和些、疾病不那么痛苦、森林和沼泽的雾气得到改善等等；而因为宗教里世界按其本质是神圣的，所以世界只是对认识的限制性、对经验直观和自己设定目的而言才被设定为不神圣的，而完整的直观和永恒的至福则被明确设定在限制性之外，即那种在道德世界秩序中应当内在、并且为了它的缘故甚至火山也应当熄灭、地震变得温和些等等、各民族[应当]不再互相以战争相侵、也不再互相掠夺等等、并且应当绝对地保持下去的限制性。
与此相反，在这种哲学里，世界既不是本源地是自然并且是神圣的，也不是按其伦理方面得到和解的，而是自在地就是某种坏的东西；不过对有限性来说，恶毕竟只是一种偶然的和任意的东西。
但如果物理的世界和伦理的世界自在地不止是坏的感性世界，如果坏不是绝对的，那么另一个绝对者、自由，也就会消失，即那种需要有一个世界、以便理性首先在其中得到实现的纯粹意志，人的全部价值也随之消失，因为这种自由只有通过否定才存在，而且只有在它所否定的东西存在时才能否定。

en: Now just as the original is not truly cognized as nature, and absolute reason is not truly cognized as being in itself and not first becoming in infinite progress, so too the relation of difference is not cognized according to its truth; for this is conceived as an in-itself and therefore is not to be sublated.
